MICHAEL ARTHUR R. CAMINA 1 0 SEP 2014 City Legal Officer Office of the City Legal Officer Caloocan City Dear Atty. Camina: BIYAHENG PINOY TAPAT NA PALAXAD, MAUNL.AD s. 2014 2014 This refers to your 15 August 2014 letter requesting legal opinion on the following: a) Whether or not the enactment of Caloocan City Ordinance No. 0535, s. constitutes sufficient basis for the City Government to enter into a Joint Venture (JV) Agreement with a qualified winning bidder for the construction, management and operation of the new Maypajo Public Market and Commercial Complex; and b) Whether or not the City still needs to comply with the requirements provided for under the Build Operate and Transfer (BOT) Law, i.e., RA 6976, as amended by RA 7718 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations. The following are the discussions relative to your query: Sufficienc T to a in n Cit r with a qualified winning bidder Before addressing the query, it should be underscored that this Department is devoid of the authority to pass upon the sufficiency, financial/economic advantage, and legality of the terms and conditions of the Ordinance. Nonetheless, this Department is not precluded from rendering its comments/observations on the matter in line with its power of supervision over local government units. As previously opined in DILG Legal Opinion No. IO, s. 2014, LGUs have the discretion in prescribing the requirements, procedures, and conditions for local joint ventures through local legislation as affirmed by the DOJ in its Opinion No. 018, s. 2012, dated 03 April 2012, viz.:

"Firstly, the . power .of LGUs to enter into JVs is provided under Section 351 Of the Code in relation to Sections 17, 222 (a) (5), (c) and (d) thereof The LGUs' full autonomy in the exercise of their proprietary functions is underscored therein subject to certain limitations that are imposed by the Code itself or by other applicable laws. The Supreme Court En Banc in Leopoldo T. Bacani, et al., vs. National Coconut Authority, Inc., et al., (G.R. No. L-9657. 29 November 1956) defined proprietary/ministrant functions as those that are undertaken only by way of advancing the general interests of society, and are merely optional. Hence, LGUs may enter into JV agreements/contracts in pursuit of their proprietary functions subject to the prior authorization of the sanggunian and the limitations imposed by applicable laws. Secondly, we sustain our opinion that in the absence of a statute and explicit guidelines on LGU JVs with the private sector, LGUs may, at their option, enter into joint venture arrangements with the private sector using the guidelines issued by the NEDA although LGUs are excluded from the coverage thereof. They may likewise adopt the rules and procedures set forth in the "Proposed PPP Code for Local Governments: Annotated" by Certified PPP Specialist Atty. Alberto C. Agra through the enactment ofan ordinance. The LGUs' discretion in prescribing the requirements, procedures and conditions for local joint ventures through local legislation was affirmed by the DOJ in its Opinion No. 018, s. 2012 dated 03 April 2012, viz.: "xxx Thus local government are free to prescribe the requirements, procedures and conditions for local joint ventures provided no law is violated. no law on Joint Ventures pertaining to local government. In the same vein, local governments may enact their own Public- Private Partnership (PPP) Code or omnibus ordinance outlining, among others, all applicable modalities. Thus, local government, through legislation, can allow unsolicited proposals in the selection of a private sector partner. A local government through enabling ordinance is free to address local concerns without an enabling statute, pmvided no statue is infringed. " Lastly, as to LGUs with no existing PPP Ordinance, their discretionary adoption of the 2008 NEDA JV Guidelines, which excludes LGUs from its coverage, does not operate as an automatic acquiescence in the adoption of the 2013 NEDA JV Guidelines, which also excludes LGUs from its coverage. The LGUs' discretion on this score is consistent with the state policy of local autonomy and is in line with the operative principle of decentralization and the national goal of propelling social and economic growth and development through the active participation of the private sector. " Clearly, the City may enter into a JV Agreement for the construction, management and operation of the new Maypajo Public Market and Commercial Complex following the requirements, procedures and conditions as set forth in its duly enacted ordinance. Com liance with the mremen provided for under the BOT Law In DILG Legal Opinion No. 47, s. 2012, this Department opined that a JV is a recognized contractual arrangement separate from the modes and variants under the BOT law, viz: "a. Land reclamation project is an eligible project to be undertaken under a PPP scheme where the financing and operation thereof can be wholly or pertly implemented by the private sector, and this covered by the BOT Law and its implementing rules. Under the expanded mandate of PPP Center pursuant to Executive Order No. 8 issued on 08 September 2010, a joint venture (J V) is a recognized contractual arrangement separate front the modes and variants under the BOT Hence, by necessary implication, there is no need to comply with the requirements under the BOT Law as the requirements, procedures and conditions for the implementation of a BOT contractual arrangement is separate and distinct from a JV Agreement which is

governed by the LGUs' own PPP Code or omnibus ordinance. Nonetheless, in case of deficiency (of the LGUs' PPP Code or omnibus ordinance), the provisions of the BOT Law and the Revised Guidelines and Procedures for Entering into Joint Venture (JV) Agreements between Government and Private Entities suppletorily applies. On a final note, it should be emphasized that the foregoing discussions should not in any way be construed as a form of validation of the JV selection process adopted and the actual procedures followed or implemented by the City of Caloocan. We hope to have enlightened you on the foregoing. Very truly yours, A TERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary DIIG-OUSLG 201 «»02705
